newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss union rejects bid to block telecoms selloff.
newsitem.headline: Swiss union rejects bid to block telecoms selloff.

text.p: A major labour union at Swiss Telecom said it would not join an effort to mount a referendum aiming to block Telecom's planned privatisation, but a leftist political party may still seek a public vote on the matter.
"We have decided we do not want to ask the public to vote on this," said Hans Uli Ruchti, general secretary of the PTT Union, which represents 30,000 Telecom workers.
Union delegates reached the decision at a special meeting in Berne on Friday, Ruchti said.
He said the meeting was held in response to urging from the leftist Workers Party (PdA), which wants to mount a referendum blocking liberalisation of the state telecommunications agency.
PdA President Jean Spielmann said his party would continue to seek support for a referendum from other political groups.
"I am convinced there will be a referendum," he said.

The Swiss government and parliament have approved a package of legislation designed to overhaul the state Post, Telephone and Telegraph (PTT) authority and to partially privatise telecommunications activities.
The reform is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 1998, in line with the European Union's telecommunications market liberalisation.

Critics of the Swiss reforms have argued that customers in remote areas could lose service. They are also concerned that the quality of service and pricing would vary from region to region as the result of planned reforms.
